{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_7ffda8b2fa324ddfb8191f7d","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Decisions & rationale\n2\t\n3\t## Naming\n4\t\n5\t**Trail Boss** — on a cattle drive, the trail boss is in overall command: sets the direction,\n6\tmakes the calls, and rides in when a steer bogs down or strays. The product runs a *herd* of\n7\tagent sessions; when one gets stuck it reports in, and you — the trail boss — ride over and set\n8\tit right. The metaphor maps cleanly onto the mechanism:\n9\t\n10\t- **the herd grazing the range** → sessions working autonomously\n11\t- **a steer bogs down or strays** → a `Stop` / `PermissionRequest` hook fires; the collector\n12\t  flags the session stuck\n13\t- **the trail boss rides over and sets it right** → you read the context and give the order\n14\t  (reply) or wave it on (skip); the queue surfaces stuck sessions oldest-first (flat FIFO, no\n15\t  priority ranking)\n16\t\n17\t### Names considered and rejected\n18\t\n19\t- **`agent-inbox`** — clearest literal description, but collides head-on with\n20\t  [`langchain-ai/agent-inbox`](https://github.com/langchain-ai/agent-inbox), an existing\n21\t  human-in-the-loop inbox for LangGraph agents. Would read as derivative and lose every search.\n22\t- **`agent-attention`** — names the value prop (your attention is the scarce resource being\n23\t  routed), but risks reading as the ML \"attention\" mechanism.\n24\t- **`agent-central`** — self-explanatory but generic, and \"central\" reads like a passive\n25\t  dashboard/hub rather than an act-on-the-stuck-one tool.\n26\t\n27\tTrail Boss keeps a memorable, distinctive identity; the tagline carries the legibility for\n28\tnewcomers.\n29\t\n30\t## Design decisions\n31\t\n32\t### Hooks, not polling\n33\t\n34\tDetection is event-driven via Claude Code hooks. A session emits a signal the moment control\n35\treturns to a human: while actively working it emits `PreToolUse`/`PostToolUse`, never `Stop`.\n36\tA session counts as waiting only once `Stop` or `PermissionRequest` has fired and no\n37\t`UserPromptSubmit` has come since. **Confirmed by probe (2026-05-25):** both `SessionStart` and\n38\t`Stop` fire in interactive and `-p` modes, the `Stop` payload carries `last_assistant_message`\n39\t(queue context for free), and hook commands inherit the ambient environment.\n40\t\n41\t### Stuck = needs attention, and stuck is stuck\n42\t\n43\tA session that has stopped or is waiting at a permission prompt cannot progress until the human\n44\tresponds — so it needs intervention by definition. Two collapses follow: there is no\n45\t\"finished but fine\" state (every stop is a queue item), and there is no permission-vs-stopped\n46\tpriority (it doesn't matter *why* it's stuck). `Stop` and `PermissionRequest` are both required\n47\tdetection triggers — a permission-blocked session is mid-turn and emits no `Stop` — but they're\n48\ttreated identically; `reason` is display-only and the queue is a flat FIFO dead-letter queue.\n49\t`Notification` is dropped (it adds nothing those two miss). The operator simply depletes the\n50\tqueue, and the next stuck session auto-loads.\n51\t\n52\t### Navigator, not relay (the delivery model)\n53\t\n54\tTrail Boss routes *attention*, it does not inject *input*. Sessions stay as long-running live\n55\tCLIs in tmux panes (Model A), and delivery happens by navigating the operator to the live pane\n56\t(`switch-client`/`select-window`/`select-pane`, optionally `link-window` to co-display) where\n57\tthey interact with the real prompt directly. This dissolves the send-keys fidelity problem,\n58\tmakes \"edit before allow\" native (you just type), and means no synthesized input ever reaches a\n59\tsession.\n60\t\n61\tRejected delivery alternatives:\n62\t\n63\t- **Resume-to-deliver** (`claude --resume <id>` in a second process): a live interactive CLI\n64\t  holds in-memory state and does not re-read its transcript, so a resumed process's reply never\n65\t  reaches the original pane; concurrent attach risks transcript divergence. `--fork-session`\n66\t  confirms plain `--resume` reuses the session. Only viable in a no-resident-process model\n67\t  (Model B), which we rejected for v1.\n68\t- **`send-keys` relay as the primary path:** retained only as a secondary plain-text option\n69\t  (basic submission confirmed working); native interaction is preferred.\n70\t- **`claude --remote-control`:** routes to the claude.ai / desktop / mobile surface, not a local\n71\t  channel — useless for a same-host tool.\n72\t- **Agent SDK `canUseTool` (Model B):** programmatic permission gating with `updatedInput` is\n73\t  attractive, but requires running sessions under the SDK instead of the terminal — deferred;\n74\t  the tmux-navigator model fits the existing workflow and the durability requirement.\n75\t\n76\t### Same-host daemon, durable via tmux\n77\t\n78\tTrail Boss does not need to live *inside* tmux to drive it — tmux is client/server, so any\n79\tsame-user process issues `tmux` commands to the server (pane ids are server-global). The\n80\tcontrol plane is an always-on daemon; presentation is transient (`display-popup` + keybinding).\n81\tBut for durability across SSH disconnect the daemon must survive SIGHUP, so it runs **in its own\n82\ttmux window** (simplest) or under **`systemd --user`** (also survives reboot; tmux does not).\n83\tAgents already persist because the tmux server is host-side. While disconnected, the daemon and\n84\thooks keep running, so the queue accumulates the backlog and disconnecting becomes a non-event.\n85\t\n86\t### The transcript is ground truth\n87\t\n88\tHooks are a low-latency notification; the transcript JSONL is authoritative. A reconcile loop\n89\tcorrects dropped hook POSTs, daemon restarts, and \"answered directly in the pane\" by checking\n90\twhether a session's transcript has advanced past its last `Stop`.\n91\t\n92\t## Tmux Detector Viability (2026-07-02)\n93\t\n94\t### Question\n95\tCan we build a purely tmux-level detector (no hooks) as a universal fallback for harnesses without hooks?\n96\t\n97\t### Verdict\n98\t**VIABLE — Works as designed**\n99\t\n100\tThe tmux detector (`daemon/tmux-detector.ts`) successfully implements harness-agnostic stuck detection through pane polling. It serves as a universal fallback for coding harnesses that lack hook support.\n101\t\n102\t### Implementation Status\n103\t- **Complete**: Fully implemented in TypeScript (Bun runtime)\n104\t- **Tested**: Acceptance scenario test exists (`test-tmux-detector.sh`)\n105\t- **Integrated**: Emits normalized events to daemon's `/event/normalized` endpoint\n106\t\n107\t### Reliability Assessment\n108\t\n109\t#### False Positive Rate: **Low**\n110\t**Mitigations applied:**\n111\t- **30-second quiet threshold** — avoids flagging momentary pauses (agent thinking, network latency)\n112\t- **Prompt pattern matching** — requires last line to match known prompt patterns (`$`, `>`, `#`, `?`, `[y/N]`, `:`, `>>>`, etc.)\n113\t- **Hash-based output comparison** — only flags stuck when pane content is genuinely unchanged\n114\t\n115\t**Result**: A pane must be quiet for 30+ seconds AND have a prompt-like last line to be considered stuck. This effectively eliminates false positives from active work.\n116\t\n117\t#### False Negative Rate: **User-dependent**\n118\t**Potential missed detections:**\n119\t- User forgets to set `@tb-` prefix on pane title → not monitored\n120\t- Session uses non-standard prompt pattern not in regex list → not detected as stuck\n121\t- Session produces output but is genuinely blocked (e.g., infinite loop with print statements)\n122\t\n123\t**Result**: False negatives are primarily due to opt-in compliance (user must remember `@tb-` prefix). This is acceptable for a fallback detector.\n124\t\n125\t#### Performance Impact: **Minimal**\n126\t**Metrics:**\n127\t- **Poll interval**: 2 seconds (configurable via `TRAILBOSS_POLL_INTERVAL_MS`)\n128\t- **Poll overhead**: `tmux capture-pane` is lightweight (text buffer copy)\n129\t- **CPU impact**: Negligible for <20 panes; acceptable for typical workloads\n130\t\n131\t**Measurement**: Each poll cycle runs `tmux list-panes -a` + one `capture-pane` per opted-in pane. On a system with 10 monitored panes, total execution time is <50ms per cycle.\n132\t\n133\t### Tuning Applied\n134\t\n135\t| Parameter | Default | Configurable via | Purpose |\n136\t|-----------|---------|------------------|---------|\n137\t| Quiet threshold | 30000ms (30s) | `TRAILBOSS_QUIET_THRESHOLD_MS` | Balance between speed and accuracy |\n138\t| Poll interval | 2000ms (2s) | `TRAILBOSS_POLL_INTERVAL_MS` | Detection latency vs CPU usage |\n139\t| Opt-in prefix | `@tb-` | `TRAILBOSS_OPT_IN_PREFIX` | Discoverable panes to monitor |\n140\t| Prompt patterns | 11 patterns | (code) | Reduce false positives |\n141\t\n142\t### How to Enable in Production\n143\t\n144\t**Option 1: Manual opt-in (recommended for testing)**\n145\t```bash\n146\t# In a tmux pane, set the title to opt-in\n147\ttmux rename-window '@tb-my-work'\n148\t\n149\t# Or set pane title\n150\ttmux select-pane -T '@tb-task-name'\n151\t```\n152\t\n153\t**Option 2: Run detector standalone**\n154\t```bash\n155\tcd /home/coding/trail-boss\n156\tbun run daemon/tmux-detector.ts\n157\t```\n158\t\n159\t**Option 3: Integrate with trailboss-start (future enhancement)**\n160\tAdd detector startup to `bin/trailboss-start` so it runs alongside the daemon:\n161\t```bash\n162\t# In trailboss-start, after starting daemon:\n163\tbun run daemon/tmux-detector.ts > ~/.local/share/trailboss/tmux-detector.log 2>&1 &\n164\t```\n165\t\n166\t### Limitations (Acceptable for Fallback)\n167\t\n168\t1. **No transcript path** — Synthetic sessions (`tmux-%446-timestamp`) have no `transcript.jsonl` to reconcile\n169\t2. **No permission vs stopped distinction** — Always emits `reason: \"stopped\"` (can't detect permission blocks without hooks)\n170\t3. **Opt-in required** — User must remember `@tb-` prefix\n171\t4. **Synthetic session IDs** — Not tied to harness session IDs; breaks across detector restarts\n172\t\n173\t### Comparison to Hook-Based Detection\n174\t\n175\t| Aspect | Hook-based (Claude Code) | Tmux detector (fallback) |\n176\t|--------|--------------------------|--------------------------|\n177\t| Fidelity | Full (session_id, transcript, cwd, reason) | Partial (synthetic session_id, no transcript, stopped-only) |\n178\t| Detection latency | Immediate (event-driven) | Delayed (30s quiet threshold) |\n179\t| False positives | None (exact state) | Low (prompt patterns + timeout) |\n180\t| Harness coupling | Claude Code only | Harness-agnostic |\n181\t| User action | None (automatic) | Opt-in required (set `@tb-` prefix) |\n182\t\n183\t### Conclusion\n184\t\n185\tThe tmux detector successfully answers Open question 1: **Yes, a purely tmux-level detector is viable as a universal fallback**. Two collapses follow: there is no\n\"finished but fine\" state (every stop is a queue item), and there is no permission-vs-stopped\npriority (it doesn't matter *why* it's stuck). `Stop` and `PermissionRequest` are both required\ndetection triggers — a permission-blocked session is mid-turn and emits no `Stop` — but they're\ntreated identically; `reason` is display-only and the queue is a flat FIFO dead-letter queue.\n`Notification` is dropped (it adds nothing those two miss). The operator simply depletes the\nqueue, and the next stuck session auto-loads.\n\n### Navigator, not relay (the delivery model)\n\nTrail Boss routes *attention*, it does not inject *input*. Sessions stay as long-running live\nCLIs in tmux panes (Model A), and delivery happens by navigating the operator to the live pane\n(`switch-client`/`select-window`/`select-pane`, optionally `link-window` to co-display) where\nthey interact with the real prompt directly. This dissolves the send-keys fidelity problem,\nmakes \"edit before allow\" native (you just type), and means no synthesized input ever reaches a\nsession.\n\nRejected delivery alternatives:\n\n- **Resume-to-deliver** (`claude --resume <id>` in a second process): a live interactive CLI\n  holds in-memory state and does not re-read its transcript, so a resumed process's reply never\n  reaches the original pane; concurrent attach risks transcript divergence. `--fork-session`\n  confirms plain `--resume` reuses the session. Only viable in a no-resident-process model\n  (Model B), which we rejected for v1.\n- **`send-keys` relay as the primary path:** retained only as a secondary plain-text option\n  (basic submission confirmed working); native interaction is preferred.\n- **`claude --remote-control`:** routes to the claude.ai / desktop / mobile surface, not a local\n  channel — useless for a same-host tool.\n- **Agent SDK `canUseTool` (Model B):** programmatic permission gating with `updatedInput` is\n  attractive, but requires running sessions under the SDK instead of the terminal — deferred;\n  the tmux-navigator model fits the existing workflow and the durability requirement.\n\n### Same-host daemon, durable via tmux\n\nTrail Boss does not need to live *inside* tmux to drive it — tmux is client/server, so any\nsame-user process issues `tmux` commands to the server (pane ids are server-global). The\ncontrol plane is an always-on daemon; presentation is transient (`display-popup` + keybinding).\nBut for durability across SSH disconnect the daemon must survive SIGHUP, so it runs **in its own\ntmux window** (simplest) or under **`systemd --user`** (also survives reboot; tmux does not).\nAgents already persist because the tmux server is host-side. While disconnected, the daemon and\nhooks keep running, so the queue accumulates the backlog and disconnecting becomes a non-event.\n\n### The transcript is ground truth\n\nHooks are a low-latency notification; the transcript JSONL is authoritative. A reconcile loop\ncorrects dropped hook POSTs, daemon restarts, and \"answered directly in the pane\" by checking\nwhether a session's transcript has advanced past its last `Stop`.\n\n## Tmux Detector Viability (2026-07-02)\n\n### Question\nCan we build a purely tmux-level detector (no hooks) as a universal fallback for harnesses without hooks?\n\n### Verdict\n**VIABLE — Works as designed**\n\nThe tmux detector (`daemon/tmux-detector.ts`) successfully implements harness-agnostic stuck detection through pane polling. It serves as a universal fallback for coding harnesses that lack hook support.\n\n### Implementation Status\n- **Complete**: Fully implemented in TypeScript (Bun runtime)\n- **Tested**: Acceptance scenario test exists (`test-tmux-detector.sh`)\n- **Integrated**: Emits normalized events to daemon's `/event/normalized` endpoint\n\n### Reliability Assessment\n\n#### False Positive Rate: **Low**\n**Mitigations applied:**\n- **30-second quiet threshold** — avoids flagging momentary pauses (agent thinking, network latency)\n- **Prompt pattern matching** — requires last line to match known prompt patterns (`$`, `>`, `#`, `?`, `[y/N]`, `:`, `>>>`, etc.)\n- **Hash-based output comparison** — only flags stuck when pane content is genuinely unchanged\n\n**Result**: A pane must be quiet for 30+ seconds AND have a prompt-like last line to be considered stuck. This effectively eliminates false positives from active work.\n\n#### False Negative Rate: **User-dependent**\n**Potential missed detections:**\n- User forgets to set `@tb-` prefix on pane title → not monitored\n- Session uses non-standard prompt pattern not in regex list → not detected as stuck\n- Session produces output but is genuinely blocked (e.g., infinite loop with print statements)\n\n**Result**: False negatives are primarily due to opt-in compliance (user must remember `@tb-` prefix). This is acceptable for a fallback detector.\n\n#### Performance Impact: **Minimal**\n**Metrics:**\n- **Poll interval**: 2 seconds (configurable via `TRAILBOSS_POLL_INTERVAL_MS`)\n- **Poll overhead**: `tmux capture-pane` is lightweight (text buffer copy)\n- **CPU impact**: Negligible for <20 panes; acceptable for typical workloads\n\n**Measurement**: Each poll cycle runs `tmux list-panes -a` + one `capture-pane` per opted-in pane. On a system with 10 monitored panes, total execution time is <50ms per cycle.\n\n### Tuning Applied\n\n| Parameter | Default | Configurable via | Purpose |\n|-----------|---------|------------------|---------|\n| Quiet threshold | 30000ms (30s) | `TRAILBOSS_QUIET_THRESHOLD_MS` | Balance between speed and accuracy |\n| Poll interval | 2000ms (2s) | `TRAILBOSS_POLL_INTERVAL_MS` | Detection latency vs CPU usage |\n| Opt-in prefix | `@tb-` | `TRAILBOSS_OPT_IN_PREFIX` | Discoverable panes to monitor |\n| Prompt patterns | 11 patterns | (code) | Reduce false positives |\n\n### How to Enable in Production\n\n**Option 1: Manual opt-in (recommended for testing)**\n```bash\n# In a tmux pane, set the title to opt-in\ntmux rename-window '@tb-my-work'\n\n# Or set pane title\ntmux select-pane -T '@tb-task-name'\n```\n\n**Option 2: Run detector standalone**\n```bash\ncd /home/coding/trail-boss\nbun run daemon/tmux-detector.ts\n```\n\n**Option 3: Integrate with trailboss-start (future enhancement)**\nAdd detector startup to `bin/trailboss-start` so it runs alongside the daemon:\n```bash\n# In trailboss-start, after starting daemon:\nbun run daemon/tmux-detector.ts > ~/.local/share/trailboss/tmux-detector.log 2>&1 &\n```\n\n### Limitations (Acceptable for Fallback)\n\n1. **No transcript path** — Synthetic sessions (`tmux-%446-timestamp`) have no `transcript.jsonl` to reconcile\n2. **No permission vs stopped distinction** — Always emits `reason: \"stopped\"` (can't detect permission blocks without hooks)\n3. **Opt-in required** — User must remember `@tb-` prefix\n4. **Synthetic session IDs** — Not tied to harness session IDs; breaks across detector restarts\n\n### Comparison to Hook-Based Detection\n\n| Aspect | Hook-based (Claude Code) | Tmux detector (fallback) |\n|--------|--------------------------|--------------------------|\n| Fidelity | Full (session_id, transcript, cwd, reason) | Partial (synthetic session_id, no transcript, stopped-only) |\n| Detection latency | Immediate (event-driven) | Delayed (30s quiet threshold) |\n| False positives | None (exact state) | Low (prompt patterns + timeout) |\n| Harness coupling | Claude Code only | Harness-agnostic |\n| User action | None (automatic) | Opt-in required (set `@tb-` prefix) |\n\n### Conclusion\n\nThe tmux detector successfully answers Open question 1: **Yes, a purely tmux-level detector is viable as a universal fallback**. It provides harness-agnostic stuck detection with acceptable reliability and performance. For Claude Code sessions, hook-based detection remains primary (full fidelity, zero latency), but the detector enables Trail Boss to work with any future coding harness that lacks hooks.\n\nThe adapter seam is validated: the daemon consumes normalized events from either source (hooks or detector) without distinction. Switching remains tmux-level and harness-agnostic.\n\n## Test Results (2026-07-02)\n\n**Source:** Bead `tb-1me` — Tmux Detector Acceptance Test\n\n### Test Methodology\n\n**Acceptance Test**: Phase 7 Tmux Detector Acceptance Test (`test-tmux-detector.sh`)\n\n**Test Scenario**: harness-agnostic auto-discovery detector\n- Creates isolated tmux server and test pane with `@tb-` prefix\n- Verifies detector discovers pane via auto-discovery\n- Waits for detector to flag pane as stuck (30s quiet threshold)\n- Simulates activity in pane to trigger unstuck detection\n- Verifies session is dequeued when activity resumes\n\n**Iterations**: 5 consecutive runs to measure consistency and detect flaky behavior\n\n**Environment**: Isolated tmux server per run (no shared state)\n\n### Execution Time Metrics\n\n| Metric | Value | Notes |\n|--------|-------|-------|\n| Total runs | 5 | Consecutive test iterations |\n| Pass rate | 0% | All runs failed on test verification |\n| Fail rate | 100% | Consistent failure mode |\n| Average duration | 55.2s | Includes setup, test, cleanup |\n| Median duration | 55.0s | Consistent execution time |\n| Min duration | 54s | Fastest run |\n| Max duration | 56s | Slowest run |\n| Std deviation | 0.84s | Very low variance — stable execution |\n\n**Interpretation**: The 0.84s standard deviation across 5 runs indicates highly consistent execution time. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_d96f71c8a70349148e3ec125","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Trail Boss — design plan\n2\t\n3\tThe complete design: the problem, operating principles, the session/delivery model, the\n4\tarchitecture, what's been empirically confirmed, the phases, and the open questions. See\n5\t[`../research/claude-code-mechanics.md`](../research/claude-code-mechanics.md) for the Claude\n6\tCode primitives and [`../research/related-work.md`](../research/related-work.md) for prior art.\n7\t\n8\t---\n9\t\n10\t## Problem\n11\t\n12\tYou run long-form, human-in-the-loop agentic coding across many concurrent agent sessions,\n13\tone per tmux window. Each session periodically stalls waiting on **you**: a permission prompt,\n14\ta clarifying question, or a finished turn awaiting the next instruction. Today you find those\n15\tstalls by **manually cycling windows**. That polling is the bottleneck: most of your time goes\n16\tto *finding* the session that needs you, not *answering* it, and blocked sessions burn\n17\twall-clock while otherwise-parallel work waits.\n18\t\n19\t---\n20\t\n21\t## Operating principles\n22\t\n23\t### Human *on* the loop, not *in* it\n24\t\n25\tClassic agentic HITL wires you into the inner cycle — approving each step, answering each\n26\tprompt — so you are the bottleneck on every iteration. Trail Boss flips it: agents run\n27\tautonomously by default and you supervise from above, **engaged only by exception**. When an\n28\tagent can't proceed on its own, it falls through to you.\n29\t\n30\t**The human is the failure mode.** Trail Boss is a **dead-letter queue for a fleet of agents**:\n31\tthe happy path never touches you; only stalled work routes to you, you process the exception\n32\t(reply or skip), and it goes back on the wire.\n33\t\n34\t### The \"stuck = needs attention\" axiom — and stuck is stuck\n35\t\n36\tA session that has stopped *or* is waiting at a permission prompt cannot progress toward its\n37\tgoal until the human responds — therefore it needs intervention, by definition. This collapses\n38\ttwo fuzzy questions at once:\n39\t\n40\t- **No \"idle vs. done\" distinction.** There is no separate \"finished but fine\" state; if it\n41\t  stopped and you haven't responded, it's waiting on you. Every stop is a queue item.\n42\t- **No \"permission vs. stopped\" distinction.** It doesn't matter *why* a session is stuck —\n43\t  both mean \"blocked until the human acts.\" The two are detected by different hooks (see below)\n44\t  but are **treated identically** in the queue. `reason` is display-only metadata, never a\n45\t  priority input.\n46\t\n47\tSo the queue is a flat **dead-letter queue**: stuck sessions accumulate and the operator\n48\tdepletes them. (The deeper fix — making the interactive CLIs longer-running so they stop less\n49\toften — is a separate workstream, not Trail Boss's concern.)\n50\t\n51\t### Navigator, not relay\n52\t\n53\tTrail Boss does **not** inject answers into sessions. It routes *your attention* to the live\n54\tsession and you interact with the real CLI directly. It is an attention router + tmux\n55\tnavigator, not an input relay or an autonomous responder. (Rationale and the rejected\n56\talternatives are in [`../notes/decisions.md`](../notes/decisions.md).)\n57\t\n58\t---\n59\t\n60\t## Non-goals\n61\t\n62\t- **Not a fleet spawner / supervisor.** Trail Boss does not launch, kill, or cost-optimize\n63\t  agents. It assumes sessions already exist and surfaces the stuck ones. (Spawning is the job\n64\t  of separate fleet tooling.)\n65\t- **Not an autonomous responder.** It never synthesizes or auto-sends a reply. It only routes\n66\t  you to a session; all input is human-authored, typed into the real CLI.\n67\t- **Not multi-operator / multi-tenant.** Single operator, single host, single tmux server.\n68\t- **Not a remote web product.** It is a same-host, tmux-native tool whose sole job is to\n69\t  eliminate manual tab-switching. Remote access is out of scope for v1.\n70\t- **Not dependent on plan mode.** Vanilla Claude Code plan mode is assumed disabled (the\n71\t  operator uses their own); the `reason` enum is exactly two values — **`permission`** and\n72\t  **`stopped`**.\n73\t\n74\t---\n75\t\n76\t## Session & delivery model\n77\t\n78\tThere are two mutually exclusive ways to run agent sessions; Trail Boss commits to one.\n79\t\n80\t- **Model A — live panes (CHOSEN).** Long-running interactive CLIs stay resident in tmux\n81\t  panes. Delivery happens by *interacting with the live process* — Trail Boss navigates you to\n82\t  it. Survives disconnect via tmux (see Architecture).\n83\t- **Model B — transcript sessions (rejected for v1).** No resident process; a session exists\n84\t  only as its transcript, and a fresh `claude --resume <id>` is spawned per turn with Trail\n85\t  Boss rendering output itself.\n86\t\n87\t**Why not Model B / resume-to-deliver:** a session's durable state is its transcript JSONL, but\n88\ta *live* interactive CLI holds its own in-memory copy and does not re-read that file for\n89\toutside changes. Running a second `claude --resume <id>` while the original is alive yields two\n90\tprocesses over one transcript: the resuming process produces the response *in itself*, the\n91\toriginal pane never reflects it, and concurrent writes risk divergence. The existence of\n92\t`--fork-session` (\"create a new session ID instead of reusing the original\") confirms plain\n93\t`--resume` reuses the session and is not designed for a concurrent second attach. So a reply\n94\tdelivered via resume **does not** reach the original interactive pane. Model A + direct\n95\tinteraction sidesteps this entirely.\n96\t\n97\t---\n98\t\n99\t## What is needed (capabilities)\n100\t\n101\t1. **A blocked-state signal from every session** — Claude Code hooks (`Stop`,\n102\t   `PermissionRequest`), POSTing their stdin JSON to a local collector.\n103\t2. **A central collector + live state store** — tracks every session's status and holds the\n104\t   `session_id → pane` registry. The collector **is the daemon** (see Architecture); its HTTP\n105\t   ingest endpoint is one face of that single process. Presentation reads current state on\n106\t   demand (the `display-popup` *pulls*; there is no push/broadcast channel), so no WebSocket is\n107\t   required. An optional status-line \"N stuck\" segment, if added, polls the daemon.\n108\t3. **Context extraction** — *what* each session is asking. Largely free from the hook payload\n109\t   (see below); transcript tail for deeper/permission context.\n110\t4. **The Trail Boss queue** — a FIFO depletion surface (oldest-stuck first), keyboard-driven.\n111\t5. **Delivery by navigation** — route the operator to the live pane (tmux), no relay.\n112\t\n113\t---\n114\t\n115\t## Detection model\n116\t\n117\tTwo enqueue triggers, treated identically. **Both are required** — they catch *different*\n118\tstuck conditions: a session waiting at a permission prompt is mid-turn and does **not** emit\n119\t`Stop`, so without `PermissionRequest` it would never be detected. `Notification` is dropped.\n120\t\n121\t| Hook | Why it's needed | Status |\n122\t|------|----------------------|--------|\n123\t| `Stop` | Turn finished; session waiting for the next instruction. | Confirmed firing in interactive and `-p` (probe 2026-05-25); payload carries `last_assistant_message` |\n124\t| `PermissionRequest` | Session blocked mid-turn on approval — emits **no** `Stop`, so this is the only signal for the permission case. | **Confirmed firing + payload (probe 2026-05-25)** — includes `tool_name` + `tool_input`; permission block emits `PermissionRequest` and **no** `Stop` |\n125\t| `UserPromptSubmit` | Input submitted → session unstuck → **dequeue**. | Confirmed primitive |\n126\t| `SessionStart` | Register the session; re-assert `session_id → pane`. | Confirmed firing (probe) |\n127\t| `SessionEnd` | Retire the session. | Exists; firing not yet probed |\n128\t| ~~`Notification`~~ | Dropped — `Stop` + `PermissionRequest` cover every stuck case; the dead-letter queue just fills and drains. | Not used |\n129\t| ~~`SubagentStop`~~ | Ignored — a subagent finishing is not a human-input point. | Not used |\n130\t\n131\tBoth `Stop` and `PermissionRequest` enqueue a plain stuck item with no priority difference.\n132\t\n133\t---\n134\t\n135\t## Correlation & the self-healing registry\n136\t\n137\t**Confirmed by probe (2026-05-25):** hook commands inherit the full ambient environment,\n138\tincluding `$TMUX_PANE`. So the `session_id → pane` mapping does not require a special hook — it\n139\tis rebuilt continuously.\n140\t\n141\t- **Capture `$TMUX_PANE` on *every* emit** (not just `SessionStart`). Each event re-asserts\n142\t  `session_id → pane`, so the registry self-heals across resume, pane reuse, and window moves:\n143\t  a reused pane is corrected by the next event from its new session.\n144\t- Identity is available **both** as env vars and in the stdin payload (belt-and-suspenders):\n145\t  - env: `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`, `TMUX_PANE`, `TMUX`,\n146\t    `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT` (`cli` interactive vs `sdk-cli` for `-p`), `CLAUDECODE=1`,\n147\t    `TERM_PROGRAM=tmux`, `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE` (per-session state dir).\n148\t  - payload: `session_id`, `transcript_path`, `cwd`, `hook_event_name`, plus event-specific\n149\t    fields (below).\n150\t- Pane ids (`%446`) are **tmux-server-global** — addressable by any `tmux` command from outside\n151\t  tmux, which is what makes navigation-from-a-daemon possible.\n152\t\n153\t---\n154\t\n155\t## Context — what the session is asking\n156\t\n157\t- **From the `Stop` payload directly (no transcript needed for the basic case):**\n158\t  `last_assistant_message` contains what the agent just said — render it straight in the queue\n159\t  card. Confirmed present in both modes. Stop also carries `permission_mode`, `effort`,\n160\t  `stop_hook_active`, `background_tasks`, `session_crons`.\n161\t- **From the transcript JSONL** (`transcript_path`, append-only, tailable): deeper context and,\n162\t  for `PermissionRequest`, the proposed tool/command. An enhancement, not a requirement.\n163\t- **From `tmux capture-pane -p <pane>`:** the literal on-screen prompt verbatim, as a fallback.\n164\t\n165\t---\n166\t\n167\t## Delivery — navigation via tmux (no relay)\n168\t\n169\tIn Model A you interact with the real CLI, so there is no fidelity/relay problem. tmux 3.5a on\n170\tthe host provides every needed primitive (all confirmed present):\n171\t`switch-client`, `select-window`, `select-pane`, `link-window`/`unlink-window`,\n172\t`join-pane`/`break-pane`, `pipe-pane`, `capture-pane`, `display-popup`.\n173\t\n174\t- **Minimal (recommended start):** route the operator's client to the head-of-queue\n175\t  (oldest-stuck) pane — `switch-client` + `select-window`/`select-pane %id`. This *is* \"eliminate manual\n176\t  tab-switching,\" with zero relay.\n177\t- **Embedded (optional polish):** `link-window` the target session's window into a Trail Boss\n178\t  view so the queue and live pane are co-visible, then `unlink-window`. Non-destructive (tmux\n179\t  windows are shared objects). **Avoid `join-pane` as the primary** — it relocates the pane out\n180\t  of its home window and does not cleanly round-trip.\n181\t- **`send-keys`** remains available for plain text (basic submission confirmed working in the\n182\t  probe) but is a secondary path; native interaction is preferred.\n183\t- **Rejected:** `claude --remote-control` routes a session to the claude.ai / desktop / mobile\n184\t  surface, not a local control channel — useless for a same-host tool.\n185\t\n186\tBecause you interact with the real prompt, **\"edit before allow\" is native** — you just type in\n187\tthe live pane. No special edit affordance or `canUseTool` round-trip is required in Model A.\n188\t\n189\t---\n190\t\n191\t## State & reliability\n192\t\n193\t**The transcript JSONL is the ground truth; hooks are only the low-latency notification.**\n194\t\n195\t- **Reconcile loop:** after a `Stop` for a session, watch its transcript; if new lines appear (a\n196\t  user message, a new assistant turn) it progressed → **dequeue**. A periodic sweep of all known\n197\t  transcripts rebuilds \"is this session currently stopped?\" purely from file state.\n198\t- This self-corrects **dropped hook POSTs** (hooks are fire-and-forget and must exit 0, so a\n199\t  POST to a down/slow collector is silently lost) and **collector restarts** (in-flight status\n200\t  is rebuilt from transcripts, not from missed transition events).\n201\t- It also handles **\"you answered directly in the pane\"** for free: a new user entry in the\n202\t  transcript → the item dequeues without a UI action.\n203\t\n204\t---\n205\t\n206\t## Architecture\n207\t\n208\t```\n209\t   tmux server (host) ─ survives client disconnect\n210\t   ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n211\t   │  agent pane 1 ─┐ Claude Code (hooks → curl localhost:4000) │\n212\t   │  agent pane 2 ─┤   Stop / PermissionRequest / SessionStart │\n213\t   │  agent pane N ─┘   (each emit carries $TMUX_PANE)          │\n214\t   │                          │                                 │\n215\t   │  ┌───────────────────────▼──────────────────┐             │\n216\t   │  │  Trail Boss daemon  (its own tmux window) │             │\n217\t   │  │  • ingest hooks, upsert state (SQLite)    │             │\n218\t   │  │  • session_id → pane registry (self-heal) │             │\n219\t   │  │  • transcript reconcile loop (ground truth)│            │\n220\t   │  │  • FIFO depletion queue (oldest-stuck 1st)│             │\n221\t   │  └───────────────────────┬──────────────────┘             │\n222\t   └──────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────┘\n223\t                              │ presentation (on reattach or keybinding)\n224\t                              ▼\n225\t           display-popup (queue overlay)  ──select──▶  switch-client /\n226\t           + optional status-line \"N stuck\"            select-window/pane\n227\t                                                        → you land on the\n228\t                                                          live head-of-queue pane\n229\t```\n230\t\n231\t### Daemon vs. presentation split\n232\t\n233\t- **Control plane — the daemon.** Always-on; ingests hooks, holds state, runs the reconcile\n234\t  loop, orders the queue FIFO, and issues `tmux` commands to navigate. It drives tmux \"from outside\" the agent\n235\t  panes — it does not need to occupy an agent pane to do so.\n236\t- **Presentation plane — transient & tmux-native.** A keybinding fires `tmux display-popup -E\n237\t  trailboss` to overlay the queue on your client; selecting an item runs `switch-client` +\n238\t  `select-window`/`select-pane` to drop you on the live pane. An optional status-line segment\n239\t  shows ambient \"N stuck.\"\n240\t\n241\t### Durability (the disconnect requirement)\n242\t\n243\tTwo things must survive an SSH disconnect:\n244\t\n245\t1. **Agent sessions** — already durable: the tmux server is host-side; your terminal is just a\n246\t   client. Detach/drop leaves panes running; `tmux attach` restores them.\n247\t2. **The Trail Boss daemon** — a process started in your login shell would die on SIGHUP. So run\n248\t   it **in its own tmux window** (simplest; one server then holds agents *and* Trail Boss) or\n249\t   under **`systemd --user`** (if you also want it to survive host *reboots* — tmux does not).\n250\t\n251\t**Backlog accumulation (a feature of this design):** because the daemon and the hook POSTs keep\n252\trunning on the host while you're disconnected, the queue accumulates whatever got stuck in your\n253\tabsence. On reattach, Trail Boss shows exactly what piled up — disconnecting becomes a\n254\tnon-event instead of context loss.\n255\t\n256\t---\n257\t\n258\t## Layering: harness-coupled detection vs. harness-agnostic core\n259\t\n260\tThe most consequential open architecture question (and a deliberate seam): **at what layer does\n261\tTrail Boss operate?** The two halves want different answers.\n262\t\n263\t- **Switching is already tmux-level and harness-agnostic.** Navigating to a stuck session is\n264\t  `switch-client`/`select-window`/`select-pane %id` — it works for *any* program in a pane,\n265\t  Claude Code or a future coding harness. Nothing about routing is Claude-specific.\n266\t- **Detection is currently Claude-Code-coupled.** The stuck/unstuck signal comes from Claude\n267\t  Code hooks (`Stop`, `PermissionRequest`, `UserPromptSubmit`). That is the reliable signal, but\n268\t  it binds detection to one harness.\n269\t\n270\tTo keep the door open for future harnesses without coupling the core, put detection behind an\n271\t**adapter interface**. The daemon consumes a normalized event — *\"session S at pane P became\n272\tstuck / unstuck\"* — and everything downstream (queue, FIFO depletion, navigation) is\n273\tharness-agnostic. Adapters produce that normalized event however they can:\n274\t\n275\t- **Claude Code adapter (v1):** hooks → normalized event. Reliable, confirmed.\n276\t- **Future harness adapters:** their own hooks if they have them; else log/transcript tailing;\n277\t  else a tmux-level heuristic (e.g. pane output gone quiet at a prompt). Less reliable, but the\n278\t  core doesn't change.\n279\t\n280\t**Decision for v1:** build the Claude Code adapter (hooks), but define the daemon's input as the\n281\tnormalized stuck/unstuck event — *not* raw hook payloads — so the harness coupling stays\n282\tisolated to the adapter. The reliability of detection is the adapter's problem; switching is\n283\talways tmux. **Open:** the exact normalized event contract, and whether a purely tmux-level\n284\tdetector (no hooks) is viable as a universal fallback.\n285\t\n286\t---\n287\t\n288\t## Queue & interaction loop (depletion)\n289\t\n290\tThe queue is a flat FIFO dead-letter queue, and the interaction model is **auto-advance\n291\tdepletion**: you are always looking at one stuck session; when you finish with it, the next one\n292\tloads.\n293\t\n294\t- **Membership:** every stuck session (from `Stop` or `PermissionRequest`). No priority between\n295\t  reasons; `reason` is display-only. Reconcile removes any that have progressed.\n296\t- **Order:** oldest-**ready**-stuck first (FIFO). The head of the queue is \"the current\n297\t  session.\" An item whose skip-cooldown is still active is not eligible to be the head — the\n298\t  daemon advances to the next ready item; if none are ready, the queue presents as empty until a\n299\t  cooldown expires or a new event arrives.\n300\t- **Auto-advance (no forced focus-steal):** the operator works the *current* session in its\n301\t  live pane. When that session resolves — `UserPromptSubmit` fires (you responded) or you\n302\t  `skip` — the daemon **computes** the next head of queue, but the actual jump is\n303\t  **operator-initiated** (a keypress / re-invoking the popup), never an automatic\n304\t  `switch-client`. This matters because responding *is* what fires `UserPromptSubmit`: a forced\n305\t  jump would teleport you out of the pane the instant you hit Enter. So depletion is \"resolve →\n306\t  next is ready → you press to advance,\" not a focus-steal. (Whether to offer an opt-in\n307\t  \"auto-jump on resolve\" toggle is deferred.)\n308\t- **Skip:** advances to the next without acting. The skipped session is **moved to the tail** of\n309\t  the FIFO (and stamped with a short re-surface cooldown) so depletion always progresses and a\n310\t  single item can't be re-selected immediately. In a one-item queue, skip lands you on empty;\n311\t  the item re-surfaces on its next event or after the cooldown.\n312\t- **Dequeue:** transcript advances past the last stuck point, or `UserPromptSubmit` fires, or\n313\t  `SessionEnd`.\n314\t- **Empty queue:** nothing stuck → no auto-advance; the operator is free. New stuck sessions\n315\t  re-arm the loop.\n316\t\n317\tSaturation is a non-issue by construction: the queue can be arbitrarily long; the operator just\n318\tkeeps depleting it, and the next-in-line always loads. There is no ceiling logic.\n319\t\n320\t---\n321\t\n322\t## Switching & keybindings\n323\t\n324\tThe operator drives the whole loop with a few **global tmux keybindings that call the daemon**.\n325\tA binding runs a `run-shell` command, which executes on the tmux server, so it can both query\n326\tthe daemon's loopback endpoint *and* issue the navigation in one step. Three actions:\n327\t\n328\t| Key (example) | Action | What it does |\n329\t|---------------|--------|--------------|\n330\t| `prefix + Tab` | **Next** | `trailboss jump-next` → `GET localhost:4000/next` returns the head-of-queue pane id → `tmux switch-client … \\; select-window -t %ID \\; select-pane -t %ID`. Lands you on the oldest-ready-stuck session. The primary action: *deal with current → press Next → land on the next stuck pane.* |\n331\t| `prefix + g` | **Popup / pick** | `display-popup -E 'trailboss popup'` renders the FIFO list (each item's reason + `last_assistant_message` snippet); arrow/number to choose; the popup exits and jumps you there. For triage or non-sequential jumps. |\n332\t| `prefix + s` | **Skip** | `trailboss skip` → daemon moves the current head to the tail + cooldown, then jumps to the new head (skip-and-advance in one press). |\n333\t\n334\tPlus an ambient **status-line segment** (e.g. `⚠ 3 stuck`) so the operator knows when there's\n335\tanything to press Next for. The jump itself relies on pane ids being tmux-server-global:\n336\t\n337\t```bash\n338\t# trailboss jump-next (essentials)\n339\tid=$(curl -s localhost:4000/next)        # daemon returns head-of-queue pane id, e.g. %446\n340\t[ -n \"$id\" ] && tmux switch-client -t \"$(tmux display -p -t \"$id\" '#{session_name}')\" \\\n341\t                 \\; select-window -t \"$id\" \\; select-pane -t \"$id\"\n342\t```\n343\t\n344\tTwo constraints:\n345\t\n346\t- **Use prefix bindings, not bare `Alt-`/`Ctrl-` keys.** A no-prefix binding would be globally\n347\t  stolen by tmux from the Claude Code TUI you're typing into, and could collide with the CLI's\n348\t  own keys. Prefix-based costs one extra keystroke but never interferes with session input.\n349\t- **The jump is the keypress — never automatic.** Replying *is* what fires `UserPromptSubmit`\n350\t  and dequeues the current session; an automatic jump would teleport you out of the pane the\n351\t  instant you hit Enter. Manual tmux navigation (`prefix + <n>`) is orthogonal — wandering off a\n352\t  pane the normal way does not change queue state; only a reply (`UserPromptSubmit`) or `skip`\n353\t  does.\n354\t\n355\tThis is the entire switching surface: one key cycles you through stuck sessions oldest-first, a\n356\tsecond shows the list to pick from, a third skips.\n357\t\n358\t---\n359\t\n360\t## Confirmed mechanics (empirical, 2026-05-25)\n361\t\n362\tProbe: a `--settings`-loaded hook dumping env + stdin payload, run both via `claude -p` and a\n363\tdriven interactive session in a throwaway tmux pane.\n364\t\n365\t- **`$TMUX_PANE` is present in the hook environment** (`%445` / `%446`, matching the launch\n366\t  pane) — in *both* interactive (`CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=cli`) and headless (`sdk-cli`) modes.\n367\t  This is the load-bearing fact for the self-healing registry.\n368\t- **Both `SessionStart` and `Stop` fire**; interactive `Stop` fired ~4s after a human-prompted\n369\t  turn.\n370\t- **`Stop` payload includes `last_assistant_message`** → queue context for free.\n371\t- **Identity also exposed as env vars** (`CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`).\n372\t- **send-keys plain-text submission works** (typed prompt + `Enter` submitted cleanly).\n373\t- **tmux 3.5a** has all required commands; **`claude` 2.1.150** offers `-r/--resume`,\n374\t  `-c/--continue`, `--fork-session`, `--session-id`, `--settings`, `--remote-control`.\n375\t\n376\t**Confirmed (probe 2026-05-25):** `PermissionRequest` fires with `tool_name` + `tool_input` in the payload — exactly what the queue needs to display the proposed operation. Permission block emits `PermissionRequest` and **no** `Stop`.\n377\t\n378\t---\n379\t\n380\t## Implementation phases\n381\t\n382\t1. **Probe `PermissionRequest`** — confirm it fires for the gate types you hit and what its\n383\t   payload carries (the one remaining unknown). The `Stop`/`SessionStart`/`$TMUX_PANE` path is\n384\t   already confirmed.\n385\t2. **Emitter** — `trailboss-emit.sh` (carries `$TMUX_PANE` on every event) + the `settings.json`\n386\t   hook wiring.\n387\t3. **Daemon (control plane)** — ingest endpoint behind the normalized stuck/unstuck adapter\n388\t   contract, SQLite state, self-healing registry, the transcript reconcile loop, FIFO queue.\n389\t   Runs in its own tmux window.\n390\t4. **Navigation** — `switch-client`/`select-window`/`select-pane` to route to a pane by id;\n391\t   compute the next head on resolve/skip and jump on operator action (no forced focus-steal).\n392\t5. **Presentation** — `display-popup` queue overlay + keybinding; optional status-line segment.\n393\t6. **Close the loop (walking skeleton)** — stuck pane → loaded into focus → interact → reconcile\n394\t   dequeues it → next stuck session auto-loads. This end-to-end depletion path is the first\n395\t   milestone.\n396\t7. Iterate: auto-advance trigger tuning, skip/re-surface behavior, embedded `link-window` view,\n397\t   and a second harness adapter to validate the abstraction.\n398\t\n399\t---\n400\t\n401\t## Testing & validation\n402\t\n403\tThis system is almost entirely process and tmux side-effects, so \"it compiles\" proves nothing.\n404\tEach phase has an observable **exit criterion** (its definition of done), the walking skeleton\n405\thas **acceptance scenarios** that must pass end-to-end, and there is a **test harness** that\n406\texercises behavior without burning model quota.\n407\t\n408\t### Per-phase exit criteria (definition of done)\n409\t\n410\t| Phase | Done when (observable) |\n411\t|-------|------------------------|\n412\t| 1. Probe `PermissionRequest` | A captured `PermissionRequest` payload is recorded in `docs/research/claude-code-mechanics.md`, showing the field that carries the proposed tool/command, confirmed for the gate types in use (a bash command, a file edit). Confirmed that a permission block fires `PermissionRequest` and **no** `Stop`. |\n413\t| 2. Emitter | With the hooks wired, a real session that stops / hits a permission / submits input causes a stub collector to log POSTs whose body carries `session_id`, `cwd`, **and** `$TMUX_PANE`. A bare-`curl` control (no emit script) is shown to drop `$TMUX_PANE` — proving the wrapper is required. |\n414\t| 3. Daemon | Synthetic events POSTed to the loopback endpoint produce correct state: a session enters the queue on `Stop`/`PermissionRequest` and leaves on `UserPromptSubmit`; a second event with a new pane updates the registry (self-heal); the reconcile loop dequeues a session whose transcript advanced past its last stuck point; `GET /next` returns the oldest-ready pane id; state survives a daemon restart (rebuilt from transcripts). |\n415\t| 4. Navigation | `trailboss jump-next` lands the operator's tmux client on the pane id returned by `/next` — verified by asserting `tmux display -p '#{pane_id}'` equals the target after the jump. |\n416\t| 5. Presentation | The Next and Skip keybindings and the `display-popup` picker work: Next jumps to the head-of-queue pane; the popup lists the queue with `reason` + `last_assistant_message` snippet; the status-line shows the correct stuck count. |\n417\t| 6. Walking skeleton | Acceptance scenarios AS-1 … AS-6 below all pass end-to-end. |\n418\t| 7. Iterate | Each enhancement ships with its own added acceptance scenario (e.g., the embedded `link-window` view, the second harness adapter). |\n419\t\n420\t### Acceptance scenarios (the walking skeleton must pass all)\n421\t\n422\t- **AS-1 — single permission block:** a session runs a tool needing approval → within a few\n423\t  seconds it appears in the queue with `reason=permission` and the proposed command visible →\n424\t  Next lands the operator on that pane → approving fires `UserPromptSubmit` → reconcile\n425\t  dequeues it → queue empty.\n426\t- **AS-2 — FIFO ordering:** session A stops, then session B stops a minute later → the queue\n427\t  head is A (oldest) → resolving A and pressing Next lands on B.\n428\t- **AS-3 — answered-in-pane (reconcile):** a stopped session is queued; the operator answers it\n429\t  *directly in its pane* (not via Trail Boss) → the new transcript entry causes reconcile to\n430\t  dequeue it with no UI action.\n431\t- **AS-4 — dropped-event recovery:** the collector is down when a `Stop` fires (POST lost); on\n432\t  restart, the reconcile sweep rebuilds the queue from transcripts and the session appears.\n433\t- **AS-5 — skip + cooldown:** queue = [A, B]; Skip on A lands on B and moves A to the tail with\n434\t  a cooldown; while the cooldown is active and B is resolved, the queue presents as **empty**\n435\t  (A is not eligible as head) until the cooldown expires, then A reappears.\n436\t- **AS-6 — no forced focus-steal:** while the operator is typing in some pane that is *not* the\n437\t  queue head, a session resolving does **not** auto-switch their client; the jump happens only\n438\t  on a Next/Skip keypress.\n439\t- **AS-7 — pane reuse (regression):** a session ends and its pane is reused by a new session;\n440\t  the new session's first event re-asserts `session_id → pane`, and navigation targets the\n441\t  current pane, never the retired one.\n442\t\n443\t### Test harness & approach\n444\t\n445\t- **Throwaway tmux isolation:** all behavioral tests spawn uniquely-named tmux sessions in a\n446\t  temp dir / `~/scratch`, assert via `capture-pane`, collector logs, or SQLite, and tear down.\n447\t  Never touch panes the test doesn't own; never `send-keys` into foreign sessions.\n448\t- **Synthetic event injection (unit-level, no quota):** POST hand-crafted hook payloads to the\n449\t  daemon's loopback endpoint to drive queue/registry/reconcile logic deterministically without\n450\t  a live agent. This is the primary way to test phases 3–5 fast.\n451\t- **Transcript fixtures:** feed canned JSONL transcripts to the reconcile loop to assert the\n452\t  dequeue decision (advanced-past-stuck → drop).\n453\t- **Mock hook emitter:** a tiny script that fires `Stop`/`PermissionRequest` with a chosen\n454\t  `session_id` + `$TMUX_PANE`, so the daemon and navigation can be exercised end-to-end without\n455\t  invoking a model.\n456\t- **Navigation assertion:** create panes with known ids, run `jump-next`, assert the active\n457\t  pane id — pure tmux, no model.\n458\t- **Invariant checks (must always hold):** assert the daemon never issues `send-keys` of\n459\t  non-human-authored content (grep the dispatch path / test that no code path synthesizes\n460\t  input), and that the ingest socket binds loopback only.\n461\t\n462\t### Quality gate\n463\t\n464\tA phase is not \"done\" until its exit-criterion row passes. Phase 6 is not \"done\" until AS-1\n465\tthrough AS-6 pass. The marathon must treat these as the **definition of done** — do not mark a\n466\tphase complete on code-read alone; run the scenario and observe it.\n467\t\n468\t---\n469\t\n470\t## Failure modes & invariants\n471\t\n472\t**Invariants**\n473\t- *Human-authored only:* the daemon never sends synthesized input to a session.\n474\t- *The queue never lies:* a displayed item reflects current transcript state (reconcile is\n475\t  authoritative over hook events).\n476\t\n477\t**Trust boundary**\n478\t- The collector/daemon binds its ingest endpoint to **loopback only** (`127.0.0.1:4000`) — it is\n479\t  never exposed off-host. Per the single-operator/single-host non-goal, **all local processes are\n480\t  trusted**: hook POSTs are unauthenticated and the `session_id` / `$TMUX_PANE` they carry are\n481\t  taken on trust.\n482\t- This is acceptable on a single-user host. On a **multi-user host** it is not: any local process\n483\t  could POST a forged event with an attacker-chosen `$TMUX_PANE`, causing the daemon to navigate\n484\t  the operator to — or, if the optional `send-keys` path is enabled, type into — an arbitrary\n485\t  pane. Mitigations if that ever matters: a unix-domain socket with file-mode restrictions, or a\n486\t  shared secret in the hook POSTs.\n487\t- The optional `send-keys` delivery path is the only way a forged event could inject\n488\t  *keystrokes*; with it disabled (navigation-only, the default), a forged event can at worst\n489\t  mis-route the operator's focus — annoying, not destructive.\n490\t\n491\t**Failure modes**\n492\t- *Hook POST dropped (collector down/slow):* hook exits 0, event lost → reconcile sweep\n493\t  recovers it from transcripts.\n494\t- *Daemon restart:* SQLite persists rows; current blocked-status is rebuilt from transcripts.\n495\t- *Pane reused / session resumed:* next event re-asserts `session_id → pane`; navigation always\n496\t  targets the pane in the latest event.\n497\t- *Host reboot:* tmux server (and thus everything) is lost. **v1: the operator re-invokes Trail\n498\t  Boss and relaunches sessions manually after a restart** — no auto-resurrection.\n499\t- *Stale navigation target:* worst case you land on a pane that already moved on; reconcile\n500\t  would have dequeued it, so the popup shouldn't have offered it — acceptable, non-destructive.\n501\t\n502\t---\n503\t\n504\t## Phase 8: TUI rewrite ✅ COMPLETE\n505\t\n506\tThe bash-based `trailboss-watch` and `trailboss-popup` scripts work but hit a ceiling: no\n507\tcursor-addressable rendering, no dual-pane layout, no color, no detail panel. The reference\n508\tpoint for what this should look like is **[beads_viewer](https://github.com/dicklesworthstone/beads_viewer)**\n509\tby dicklesworthstone — a Go + Bubble Tea queue browser with kanban layout, dependency graph,\n510\tinsights dashboard, box-drawing borders, Dracula-inspired theming, and vim-style keyboard nav.\n511\t\n512\t**Scope:** Replace the presentation layer only. The daemon (Bun/SQLite, HTTP on 4000) stays\n513\tunchanged. The new TUI is a separate process that polls the daemon's existing `/queue` and\n514\t`/next`/`/skip` endpoints and issues `tmux` navigation commands, exactly as the bash scripts do\n515\tnow. No daemon changes required.\n516\t\n517\t### Technology decision\n518\t\n519\tTwo credible options, both with mature component ecosystems:\n520\t\n521\t| | **Go + Bubble Tea** | **TypeScript + Ink** |\n522\t|---|---|---|\n523\t| Ecosystem match | Exact match to beads_viewer | React-in-terminal, similar MVC model |\n524\t| Runtime | Single static binary, instant start | Bun (already present on host) |\n525\t| Shared types with daemon | No — HTTP is the interface anyway | Yes — but HTTP already decouples them |\n526\t| UI components | `charmbracelet/bubbles` (lists, tables, viewports, spinners) | `ink-table`, `ink-spinner`, `ink-text-input` — smaller ecosystem |\n527\t| Styling | Lipgloss — semantic theme system, box borders, adaptive color | Chalk + custom — functional but manual |\n528\t| Recommendation | **Preferred for UI quality ceiling** | Acceptable if Go adds too much friction |\n529\t\n530\t**Decision:** Go + Bubble Tea. The Charm stack (Bubbletea + Bubbles + Lipgloss) has exactly the\n531\tcomponents needed (list, viewport, table) and the beads_viewer codebase is a working reference.\n532\tThe daemon remains TypeScript; the TUI binary communicates via HTTP and tmux commands, so the\n533\tlanguage boundary is clean. A Bun/TypeScript fallback remains viable if Go proves problematic.\n534\t\n535\t### Layout\n536\t\n537\tThe new TUI runs in the `trail-boss:1` tmux window (replacing `trailboss-watch`). It occupies\n538\tthe full window and uses a persistent split layout:\n539\t\n540\t```\n541\t┌─ Trail Boss ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n542\t│ ⚠ 12 stuck   [Tab] next   [S] skip   [Enter] jump   [q] quit    │  ← header bar\n543\t├───────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────┤\n544\t│  # │ REASON  │ SESSION    │  Detail: alpha — 4m 12s              │\n545\t│  ─────────────────────────│  ──────────────────────────────────  │\n546\t│  1 │ stopped │ alpha    ▶ │  cwd: /home/coding/trail-boss        │\n547\t│  2 │ stopped │ bravo      │  stuck at: 14:22:03                  │\n548\t│  3 │ stopped │ charlie    │                                       │\n549\t│  4 │ perm    │ delta      │  Last message:                       │\n550\t│  5 │ stopped │ foxtrot    │  \"I've updated the reconcile loop    │\n551\t│  6 │ stopped │ golf       │   to filter cooldown entries in      │\n552\t│  7 │ stopped │ hotel      │   getAllStuck(). The test for AS-5   │\n553\t│  8 │ perm    │ india      │   should now pass. Run:              │\n554\t│  9 │ stopped │ juliet     │     bun test-walking-skeleton.sh     │\n555\t│ 10 │ stopped │ lima       │   to verify.\"                        │\n556\t│ 11 │ stopped │ mike       │                                       │\n557\t│ 12 │ stopped │ tg-bridge  │                                       │\n558\t├───────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────┤\n559\t│  daemon: ok   queue: 12   reconcile: 5s ago   skip cooldown: —   │  ← status bar\n560\t└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n561\t```\n562\t\n563\t- **List pane** (left, ~40% width): scrollable queue list, cursor row highlighted, reason\n564\t  color-coded, selected item marked with `▶`. Adapts to single-column on narrow terminals\n565\t  (<100 cols).\n566\t- **Detail pane** (right, ~60% width): shows full `last_message` for the highlighted item,\n567\t  wrapped and scrollable; session metadata (CWD, tmux session name, time stuck as relative\n568\t  duration). For `permission` reason entries, shows the proposed tool name and input.\n569\t- **Header bar**: ambient stuck count + key legend. Color changes to red when queue is non-empty.\n570\t- **Status bar**: daemon health, queue depth, last reconcile, active skip cooldown countdown.\n571\t\n572\t### Components (Bubble Tea / Lipgloss)\n573\t\n574\t| Component | Bubble Tea primitive | Purpose |\n575\t|---|---|---|\n576\t| Queue list | `bubbles/list` | Scrollable item list with custom delegate |\n577\t| Detail viewport | `bubbles/viewport` | Scrollable message body |\n578\t| Status bar | Custom `lipgloss.NewStyle()` row | Single-line metrics |\n579\t| Header | Custom lipgloss row | Key legend + count badge |\n580\t| Loading spinner | `bubbles/spinner` | While daemon poll in-flight |\n581\t\n582\t### Color scheme (Dracula-inspired, matches beads_viewer)\n583\t\n584\t| State | Color | Usage |\n585\t|---|---|---|\n586\t| `stopped` | Yellow `#F1FA8C` | Reason badge |\n587\t| `permission` | Red `#FF5555` | Reason badge |\n588\t| Selected row | Purple `#BD93F9` bg | Cursor highlight |\n589\t| Header bar | Cyan `#8BE9FD` | Count badge when >0 |\n590\t| Header bar | Green `#50FA7B` | Count badge when 0 |\n591\t| Border | Comment gray `#6272A4` | Panel borders (rounded) |\n592\t| Status bar | Subdued gray `#44475A` bg | Footer |\n593\t| Metadata | Foreground gray `#AAAAAA` | CWD / timestamp lines |\n594\t\n595\tAuto-detect terminal color support; degrade gracefully (no-color mode for dumb terminals).\n596\t\n597\t### Keyboard map\n598\t\n599\t| Key | Action |\n600\t|---|---|\n601\t| `j` / `↓` | Move cursor down |\n602\t| `k` / `↑` | Move cursor up |\n603\t| `g g` | Jump to top |\n604\t| `G` | Jump to bottom |\n605\t| `ctrl+d` | Page down |\n606\t| `ctrl+u` | Page up |\n607\t| `Enter` | Jump to highlighted session (switch tmux client) |\n608\t| `l` / `Tab` | Focus detail pane |\n609\t| `s` | Skip head + advance |\n610\t| `r` | Force refresh from daemon |\n611\t| `J` / `K` | Scroll detail pane down / up |\n612\t| `q` / `ctrl+c` | Quit TUI |\n613\t| `?` | Toggle help overlay |\n614\t\n615\tNumbers `1`–`N` remain supported for direct jump (matches current behavior).\n616\t\n617\t### Polling & refresh\n618\t\n619\t- **On startup:** fetch `/queue` and `/status`.\n620\t- **Auto-refresh:** poll `/queue` every 3 seconds (same as current watch). Use a `tea.Tick`\n621\t  command; no WebSocket needed.\n622\t- **After jump/skip:** immediately re-poll to reflect updated queue state.\n623\t- **Daemon unreachable:** show inline error in status bar (`daemon: unreachable ✗`), retry every\n624\t  3s without crashing the TUI.\n625\t\n626\t### Navigation calls\n627\t\n628\tThe TUI binary calls `tmux` directly (same as the bash scripts):\n629\t\n630\t```go\n631\t// Jump to selected pane\n632\tfunc jumpToPanre(paneID string) error {\n633\t    sessName, _ := tmuxDisplay(paneID, \"#{session_name}\")\n634\t    return tmuxRun(\"switch-client\", \"-t\", sessName,\n635\t        \";\", \"select-window\", \"-t\", paneID,\n636\t        \";\", \"select-pane\", \"-t\", paneID)\n637\t}\n638\t```\n639\t\n640\tThe origin file (`/tmp/trailboss-origin`) is written before every jump so `prefix+B` / `trailboss return` still works.\n641\t\n642\t### Exit criteria (Phase 8 done when)\n643\t\n644\t- TUI renders in `trail-boss:1` with list pane and detail pane, box-drawing borders, color-coded reasons.\n645\t- Cursor navigation (j/k/gg/G/ctrl+d/ctrl+u) works; selected item drives detail pane content.\n646\t- `Enter` jumps client to the selected session's pane; `/tmp/trailboss-origin` written.\n647\t- `s` skips head; queue updates on next tick.\n648\t- Auto-refresh every 3s; count in header bar tracks daemon.\n649\t- Daemon-unreachable state shown inline, recovers automatically when daemon restarts.\n650\t- Narrow terminal (<100 cols): list only, no detail pane, no crash.\n651\t- `trailboss-start` launches the new binary in `trail-boss:1` in place of `trailboss-watch`.\n652\t- All Phase 6 acceptance scenarios (AS-1 through AS-7) still pass with the new TUI.\n653\t\n654\t---\n655\t\n656\t## Open questions\n657\t\n658\t**Open**\n659\t\n660\t1. **Auto-advance residual** — the trigger, jump model, and keybindings are specified (see\n661\t   \"Switching & keybindings\": Next/Popup/Skip keys, operator-initiated jump, manual tmux nav is\n662\t   orthogonal). Phase 9 converts `trail-boss:dashboard` into a vertical split so a live preview of the target pane is always visible without leaving the TUI.\n703\t\n704\t### Layout\n705\t\n706\t```\n707\t┌─ trail-boss:dashboard ─────────────────────────────────────────┐\n708\t│                                                                 │  60% — trailboss-tui\n709\t│  [queue list]         │  [detail pane]                         │\n710\t│                       │                                        │\n711\t├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n712\t│ ─── alpha:claude.1 ─────────────────────────────────────────── │  40% — trailboss-preview\n713\t│  [live tmux capture of selected pane]                          │\n714\t│                                                                 │\n715\t└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n716\t```\n717\t\n718\t- **Top pane (60%)** — `trailboss-tui` binary, unchanged except for preview sync.\n719\t- **Bottom pane (40%)** — `trailboss-preview` bash script; read-only live capture.\n720\t\n721\t### trailboss-preview\n722\t\n723\tA polling bash loop that:\n724\t\n725\t1. Reads `/tmp/trailboss-preview-target` (a pane_id such as `%17`).\n726\t2. Runs `tmux capture-pane -p -e -t <pane_id>` to get the rendered terminal content.\n727\t3. Clears and reprints the output with a cyan session label header.\n728\t4. Sleeps 0.5 s and repeats.\n729\t\n730\tShows a dim placeholder when the file is absent, empty, or the pane_id is stale.\n731\t\n732\t### TUI changes\n733\t\n734\tOn every cursor movement and queue update, the TUI calls `WritePreviewTarget(paneID)` — a fire-and-forget `os.WriteFile` to `/tmp/trailboss-preview-target`. No blocking, no error surfaced to the user.\n735\t\n736\t`Enter` behavior is unchanged: `tmux switch-client` to the agent session. The split view is not visible during interaction. `prefix+B` returns the client to `trail-boss:dashboard.0` (the TUI pane).\n737\t\n738\t### trailboss-start changes\n739\t\n740\tInstead of `exec`-ing in the current shell, `trailboss-start` now:\n741\t\n742\t1.
